Yes, nomograms designed to predict biochemical recurrence (BCR) can do a better job of predicting more clinically relevant prostate cancer outcomes than BCR alone. BCR is defined as a rise in prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels after treatment, but it may not always correlate with clinically significant outcomes such as metastasis or prostate cancer-specific mortality. 

Nomograms that incorporate additional variables, such as pathological features, PSA kinetics, and patient characteristics, can provide more accurate predictions of these clinically relevant outcomes. By accounting for these factors, nomograms can help identify patients at higher risk of aggressive disease progression, allowing for more personalized and effective treatment strategies.
